sections.h2: Who bills property tax inside Columbia city limits?
sections.html:
A house inside Columbia owes tax to two governments, the City of Columbia and Maury County. Owners within the corporate limits pay both.

The county Property Assessor, at 6 Public Square, phone 931-375-4001, sets values. The county portion is collected by the Trustee at 1 Public Square, phone 931-375-2201, open weekdays from 8 to 4. The city bills its own tax and keeps a lookup and payment portal on its Property Tax page.

County notices are addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. A bill that never reaches you still collects interest once it goes delinquent, because state law does not require notices to be mailed.

Columbia accepts city payments without penalty from November 1 through December 15. The City Recorder handles real and personal property under the same window.

Late charges stack up in three steps after the window closes:

  • A 0.5% charge applies through the end of December.
  • Another 0.5% accrues starting January 1.
  • From February 1, the city adds 1% for every month the balance stays open.

sections.h2: How and when do you pay Maury County tax?
sections.html:
The county calendar is longer than the city's. Payment opens in early October and stays penalty-free until the final day of February. Interest of 1.5% starts on March 1 and climbs monthly.

Partial payments are welcome, though interest applies to anything unpaid on March 1. A postmark counts as the payment date until the Trustee hands delinquent accounts to Chancery Court on April 1.

The Trustee offers several ways to pay:

  • Walk in at the office on Public Square.
  • Mail a check to Maury County Trustee at the same address.
  • Use the drop box outside the office after hours, with checks only.
  • Pay online by card or e-check; the vendor, not the county, takes a 2.5% fee.
  • Call 1-877-556-4502 to pay by phone.
  • Ask about monthly ACH debits that split the bill into equal installments.

sections.h2: Reappraisal year and how to appeal
sections.html:
Maury County reappraises every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year. Values on the Assessor's records reflect the market as it stood on January 1 of the last reappraisal year, with equalized improvement values added.

An owner who thinks the value is unfair can go to the local board of equalization, then to the State Board. The county board begins meeting June 1, and the State Board deadline is August 1 or 45 days after the county board mails its decision, whichever comes later. A challenge started after those dates belongs to the next cycle.

Columbia and Maury County tax dates
Tax eventDateOffice
City tax without penaltyNovember 1 to December 15City of Columbia
County payment periodEarly October to the end of FebruaryMaury County Trustee
County tax delinquentMarch 1, at 1.5% a monthMaury County Trustee
Delinquent accounts to courtApril 1Maury County Trustee
Relief applicationsJanuary 20City of Columbia

Help comes in two layers. A state program covers seniors, owners who are completely and permanently disabled, and disabled veteran owners with their surviving spouses. On top of that, the city gives a modest credit of up to $75 a year to qualifying seniors.

For the senior or disability route, household income for the prior year must be $38,470 or less, counting you, a spouse and anyone else named on the deed. Seniors need to have reached 65 by the end of the prior year. Disabled applicants need certification from the Social Security Administration or another qualified agency. The state program helps pay local bills and is not a separate state tax.

Veteran owners with a 100% rating, and their surviving spouses, file Form F-16 or F-16S with VA paperwork, available at the City Recorder's Office in City Hall. Every application is due January 20 of the current year, and the Trustee's staff will also help with the state forms.

Columbia had 41,690 residents in 2020 and an estimated 50,072 by mid-2025. For 2020 to 2024 the typical owner-occupied home was worth $308,700, owners lived in 63.3% of housing units and median gross rent was $1,197. Growth like that keeps buyer interest steady, and it also means tax notices change often.

sections.h2: How to estimate a Columbia tax bill by hand
sections.html:
The Assessor's method is appraised value times the ratio for the property class, then that product times the rate. A home in Tennessee's residential class uses 25%.

Divide the assessed value by 100, then multiply by the county rate and by the city rate. Get both from the Trustee and the City Recorder, since the Maury County Commission and the city council set them through their budgets.

In a reappraisal year the appraisal itself moves, so set the new notice beside last year's before you assume the total will look the same.

sections.h2: Selling a Columbia house with taxes open
sections.html:
Show a buyer the tax history up front. Request written balances from the Trustee and the City Recorder before listing. A county balance still open at April 1 goes to Chancery Court, so settle it before that date. Payments postmarked on time are honored up to then.

At closing, the title company usually collects both balances from the sale proceeds. Ask which office holds each year, and confirm that city tax, which runs on the November to December window, is paid separately from the county bill. A cash buyer will want the same paperwork, so having it ready speeds up the sale.

sections.h2: Step by step: paying off Columbia taxes at a sale
sections.html:
Two collectors and two calendars make a Columbia closing a little more involved than a county-only sale. A simple order of work keeps it tidy.

  1. Ask the Trustee at 931-375-2201 for the county balance and any delinquent years.
  2. Ask the City Recorder for the city balance, noting that the city window runs November 1 to December 15.
  3. Check whether a relief or senior credit application is pending, since those are due January 20.
  4. Give both figures to the title company so each appears on the settlement statement.
  5. Settle any county balance before April 1, when delinquent accounts move to court.

Because county notices follow the January 1 owner, the seller's name may still sit on a bill that arrives after closing. Forward it to the title company so the proration is handled in writing.

faqs.q: When is Columbia, TN city property tax due?
faqs.a: City tax is due without penalty from November 1 through December 15. After December 15, 0.5% is added through December, another 0.5% from January 1 and 1% a month from February 1.

faqs.q: When does Maury County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. County tax can be paid from the first Monday of October through the last day of February, and interest of 1.5% applies from March 1, growing monthly. Delinquent accounts go to Chancery Court on April 1.

faqs.q: Do I pay both city and county tax in Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone living within the city limits pays both. The city bills its own tax, and the Maury County Trustee bills the county portion.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. Seniors 65 or older with income of $38,470 or less can apply for state relief, and the city adds up to $75 a year for qualifying seniors. Applications are due January 20 of the current year.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about my Columbia home's value?
faqs.a: Call the Maury County Property Assessor at 931-375-4001 or visit 6 Public Square. Reappraisals happen every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year in the county.
